V3 FATAL - Artifact controls certify constructed objects, not measured behavior. index_manifest webapi section is build_manifest(themes, ...) on the same themes object as hierarchical (line 272); ir_manifest workflows are static templates with fabricated locators (test-{fam}-{i}) and compile_cost clamped into [0.002,0.092] by a formula (lines ~285-295); no TreeWalker traversal, DOM, or locator ranking executes. These attesting controls cannot distinguish a genuine compiled IR from a relabeled baseline.

V4 - Freshness gating and NC-STALE-FALSE-ACCEPT are circular. freshness_check returns task['freshness_label']=='fresh' (lines 576-577): the gate reads the hidden ground-truth staleness label, which the frozen representation forbids as a pipeline input (spec.json measurement_validity; prereg.md line 43: forbidden 'staleness label'). Gated stale false 0.0 vs ungated 1.0 is therefore guaranteed by construction and provides no evidence about the intended watermark/version-TTL mechanism. Failure mode: a broken TTL implementation would still pass this control.

(report.md line 95 interprets 0/40 as 'alias requires semantic reasoning' — that interpretation is not supported by the code, which never hashes a DOM.)

V6 - Hardcoded confidence reintroduced. conf = 0.85*max(softmax) + 0.12 + deterministic_jitter at lines 596, 612, 642, 689, 709, 750. prereg.md line 57 and spec baselines require 'no hardcoded confidence', and prereg.md line 185 lists 'hardcoded 0.85*softmax+0.12+jitter' among the rejected miscalibration patterns to be audited.
